505.title: Equity
505.tag: Equity: owners' residual claim — contributions, distributions, treasury stock, splits and spinoffs.
505.truth: Equity is whatever is left for owners after every creditor is paid. Transactions with owners — putting money in, taking it out, buying back shares — never create profit or loss, because a company cannot earn income from its own owners. Those flows go straight to equity accounts.

analogy.title: The Family Business Cookie Jar
analogy.story: When Mom puts $1,000 into the family bakery's cookie jar, the bakery didn't earn anything — it just has more of the family's own money. When the bakery hands $500 back to Dad, it didn't lose anything. Only selling bread creates profit.

recognition: Contributions from owners increase paid-in capital at the fair value of consideration received.
Distributions/dividends reduce equity when declared (liability recognized at declaration).
Treasury stock: cost method (contra-equity) or par-value method; gains/losses on reissuance go to APIC, never income (505-30-30-10).
Stock dividends < 20–25% are capitalized at fair value; larger ones are treated like splits (505-20-25).
Spinoffs to owners are recorded at carrying amount (505-60).

measurement.basis: Fair value of consideration received / carrying amounts
measurement.initial: Initial: proceeds net of direct issuance costs.
measurement.subsequent: Subsequent: not remeasured (except certain instruments classified as liabilities or temporary equity).

journalEntries.scenario: A company buys back 20,000 of its shares at $25.
journalEntries.memo: Contra-equity; reissuance above cost credits APIC.

auditTraps.q: Can a gain on reissuing treasury stock go to income?
auditTraps.a: Never — transactions in an entity's own shares go to equity (APIC).

auditTraps.q: When is a dividend a liability?
auditTraps.a: At declaration — not at record or payment date.

auditTraps.q: Stock dividend of 10% — fair value or par?
auditTraps.a: Small stock dividend (<20–25%): capitalize retained earnings at fair value. Large ones are accounted for like a split (par value or memo only).

505.propertyLens: Capital calls, distributions and promote payments to GPs/LPs are equity transactions — never revenue or expense — in multifamily partnerships.

keyParagraphs.excerpt: Gains on sales of treasury stock not previously accounted for as constructively retired shall be credited to additional paid-in capital; losses may be charged to additional paid-in capital to the extent that previous net gains from sales or retirements of the same class of stock are included therein, otherwise to retained earnings.

The number of additional shares issued as a stock dividend may be so great that it has, or may reasonably be expected to have, the effect of materially reducing the share market value. In such a situation, because the implications and possible shareholder belief discussed in paragraph 505-20-30-3 are not likely to exist, the substance of the transaction is clearly that of a stock split.
